newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ocampo rules out 4 pct 1997 GDP target.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ocampo rules out 4 pct 1997 GDP target.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Tuesday that the government's target of four percent growth in gross domestic product in 1997 was "no longer viable".

But in a conversation with Reuters, he said that he nonetheless believed that data on second quarter growth would show that Colombia had pulled out of its first recession in decades. He added that the country could achieve year-end GDP growth of between 3 percent and 3.5 percent.
"Industrial production figures in the first quarter were bad," Ocampo told Reuters, at an event to celebrate the 70th anniversary of the National Coffee Growers' Federation in Medellin.
"But all the available surveys for April and May...show a significant recovery in May. I would say that we could expect growth of as much as 2 percent in GDP in the second quarter," he added.
Colombia's industrial output fell 6.94 percent, excluding coffee processing in the first quarter, and plummeted 11.66 percent in March alone.

Coupled with poor industrial performance, Colombia found itself plunged into recession for the first time in decades at the end of the first quarter, when GDP fell by 1.22 percent. That followed a slip of 0.1 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Even if Ocampo's forecast of 2 percent growth for the second quarter is borne out in the final data, that pace would still be slower than last year's 2.4 percent growth in the same period.
Central bank chief Miguel Urrutia said he believed the recovery would begin to be seen in the second half of the year.
"The majority of observers believe there will be a recovery in the second half of this year, in the third and fourth quarters," he told Reuters.

He declined, however, to give his own year-end growth forecast, saying the central bank was using the same economic models as the National Planning Department. Planning Department chief Cecilia Lopez earlier this week spoke of GDP growth of between 3 percent and 3.5 percent this year.
Last year, Colombia's GDP grew 2.08 percent.
